rows.title: 1-Page Fit that cannot reach one page lowers the text to 9 pt without saying so
rows.summary: Now: when 1-Page Fit cannot get a résumé onto one page, it still writes the tightest step, including the 9 pt base text size, as R2-149 intends. The notice now says so: 'Still N pages at the tightest spacing and 9 pt text (was 11 pt) — shorten the content to fit one page.' Before, it said only 'Still N pages at the tightest spacing — …', so an 11 pt résumé became 9 pt without a word, and 1-Page Fit has no Undo. A résumé whose base size did not change (already at 9 pt or below, so the ladder has no size step) gets the spacing-only wording. The wording comes from fitSizeNotice (src/utils/pageFit.js), which now covers both a fit that succeeds and one that fails. DesignPanel.fitToOnePage calls it instead of building the 'Still N pages' string inline. A fit that succeeds speaks as before: nothing for spacing alone, and 'Fits on 1 page — text size A → B pt.' when the size came down. Stale tests updated with evidence: 102-r4-dux-15 expected an empty size notice for pages > 1, which was the bug itself, and the exact regex in 91-page-fit now expects the size clause, with the tightest step still asserted as stored. The looser regexes in 102-r4-dux-25 and 91-page-fit's StrictMode test ('pages at the tightest spacing', '^Still N pages') still match the new wording. No exporter, template or stored-data change.
rows.failfirst_run: 36530615541 (green: with 286b43e's diff reversed the two named files fail with '# fail 3', and they pass with it restored; named tests 35/35 in the same run: the new test, 102-r4-dux-15, 91-page-fit, r5hunt1-fit-keeps-tight-spacing, 31-contact-fields, 91-design-resets, knowledge-docs)

issues.issue: Does the notice name the wrong 'was' size? The ladder is built from {...settings, ...preset}, and the notice from settings as clicked.
issues.resolution: No change needed: the preset (fitLadder(settings)[0]) never carries fontSizeBase, so both read the same base, with the same Number.isFinite fallback to 11 pt. A fractional base (10.5) is named as 'was 10.5 pt', which is correct.

issues.issue: A base below 9 pt, or a fit with no settings, could produce 'and undefined pt text'.
issues.resolution: No change needed: the size clause needs fit.settings?.fontSizeBase to be defined and different from base. A base at or below MIN_FIT_BASE_PT adds no size step, so the spacing-only wording is used. A null fit returns ''.

issues.issue: Other tests or specs that match the old exact wording.
issues.resolution: No change needed: I grepped src, tests, cypress and e2e. Only 91-page-fit carried the exact string, and it was updated. The 102-r4-dux-25 and 91-page-fit StrictMode regexes are prefix/substring matches that still hold. docs/knowledge does not describe the notice.

issues.issue: Alternative fix: keep the original text size when no step fits.
issues.resolution: Rejected as the fix: R2-149 and the existing 91-page-fit tests keep the tightest step, 9 pt included, as intended behaviour. Stating the change fixes the silent part without reversing a tracked product decision.
Verified in the job log for run 36530615541, job 109283270503: 'fail without the fix (its diff reversed): # fail 3', then 'pass with it'.
